blocks.text: For example, ahead of a design crit, Figma Design Manager Megan Bednarczyk uses the agent to gather the background information she needs to prepare. “There’s usually a lot of context to catch up on,” she says. “What did we hear in research? What came up in Slack? What did we agree on last time?”

blocks.text: Megan starts with the designs already arranged on the board. She uses the agent and connectors to bring in feedback from previous crits and competitor examples alongside them. The agent summarizes previous feedback, the direction the team agreed on, and questions for the upcoming crit. It also adds notes highlighting patterns in the competitor examples.

blocks.text: After a team discussion in FigJam, you may have a board full of feedback to work through. The agent can pull those sticky notes and comments together into a Spec—a collaborative document that lives on the canvas. You can then review and edit the draft to guide what happens next.

blocks.text: Johnny Dallas, the engineering lead on Specs, uses the agent in FigJam to turn feedback from engineering crits into a draft spec he can review and edit before moving into implementation. “I’ll have a FigJam board that has dozens or hundreds of stickies and comments and opinions from all these smart engineers,” he says. “My job is to take that and actually turn it into code.” But sometimes, it can be hard to come back to a FigJam board after a thoughtful discussion and determine next steps. “In the past when I’ve done crits, I have to go through and read every comment. I might miss some of the quotes, or spend too much time sweating the details. There’s a lot of cleanup,” Johnny explains.

blocks.text: When you’re preparing a presentation, you need to decide what to include, how to order it, and what you want the audience to take away. The Figma agent in Figma Slides can help you with starting points and finishing touches, giving you more time to shape the narrative, communicate clearly, and prepare for the audience.

blocks.text: Start with the material you already have

inlines.text: Start with the material you already have

blocks.text: In Figma Slides, you can bring a Spec, attach supporting material, or connect relevant context, and the agent can turn it into a first pass. Jarrod Barretto, a brand designer at Figma, uses the agent this way when working on keynote presentations for Config and internal events. He starts with a script that executives have developed together, then uses the Figma agent to turn that script into slides by prompting: Break this up into individual slides so the content flows logically. The agent creates an outline he can review and edit before clicking Generate deck to create the slides. “That gives me an architecture—a starting point I can start to fill in,” he says.

blocks.text: Spend less time on manual work

blocks.text: Once you have a first draft of a presentation in Figma Slides, you can ask the agent to take over work like building charts. For example, Jarrod shares a screenshot of a spreadsheet with the agent and prompts it to populate a bar chart from that data. Previously, he’d have to manually draw a chart to scale from scratch. Now, the agent takes on that work. “I can be really precise about how I want a chart to look while letting the agent take care of the mathematical accuracy,” he says. You can also ask the agent to create a chart from scratch using data you provide.
